task_brief: Day 5 of "Theatre, Direction, and Presentation Craft" (unit 4, grade 9) is a second concept model on rehearsal process and ensemble roles. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Direct and present a rehearsed scene in a chosen private or shared format with a director’s book and an annotated rehearsal record. Today's work contributes to that by handling rehearsal process and ensemble roles at the concept model b stage, against the unit's wider topics of script analysis of public-domain or original text, character objectives and given circumstances, voice articulation and physical expression, and directing and blocking choices. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Study a second, contrasting model work for rehearsal process and ensemble roles and set it beside the first one you examined earlier in this unit. Build a comparison naming one choice the two makers share and one place they clearly diverge, with the effect of each difference described in terms a listener or viewer could verify. Then make one short study of your own that borrows the second maker's approach to rehearsal process and ensemble roles. Cite both works. Anything you did not make yourself must be public domain, openly licensed, or properly attributed. Use the attached Model A recap and contrasting Model B as the two works for comparison; no earlier source file is required. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about rehearsal process and ensemble roles, and it belongs to "Theatre, Direction, and Presentation Craft", which also covers separate topics such as script analysis of public-domain or original text. Close out with this check before you stop: State what the contrasting example of rehearsal process and ensemble roles revealed that the first one did not. At grade 9 the bar is independent work with explicit criteria set before you start, and evidence that you evaluated the finished result against those criteria rather than against how it felt.

sourceReference:
ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g9-arts-and-music-u04-l05

Lesson focus: rehearsal process and ensemble roles

Resource type: ACADEMY_ORIGINAL_MODEL

MODEL B — "The Doorway," contrasting with "The Missing Note." A begins beside the exit and says, "I know where to look." B takes one step into A's path and answers, "Knowing is not the same as checking." A turns away, pauses one count, then writes a plan. Model A uses stillness for uncertainty; Model B changes position to show conflict and choice. Use it to study rehearsal process and ensemble roles; describe evidence before judging and adapt the example rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Model A recap and contrasting Model B as the two works for comparison; no earlier source file is required.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: One shared choice and one clear divergence between the two model works are both named.
The effect of each difference is described in verifiable terms rather than as preference.
A short original study borrows the second work's approach.
Both works are cited; nothing uncredited and nothing outside public-domain or licensed use appears.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task centres an aural element (rehearsal process and ensemble roles). Provide a fully equivalent non-aural route: notated, written, or graphic representation; visual or tactile pulse (a moving marker, a tapped or felt beat); and vibration or sight-reading in place of listening. Do not require the learner to hear a pitch, interval, or timbre to demonstrate understanding of it.

Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries exactly the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording. A written or notated account of the intended performance is a full substitute.

Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting rehearsal process and ensemble roles.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for rehearsal process and ensemble roles follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for rehearsal process and ensemble roles, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to rehearsal process and ensemble roles works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of rehearsal process and ensemble roles, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking rehearsal process and ensemble roles mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply rehearsal process and ensemble roles under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on rehearsal process and ensemble roles rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
